🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-29 23:00 → 2026-09-30 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **CUDA GKR runs on GPT-2** — Jimmy Shi turned the layer-granularity GKR concept into a runnable GPT-2 experiment, giving the group its first concrete CUDA baseline to profile and extend. [tg:tawg:5053]

> **Grader bug isolated and decomposed** — Pavlo surfaced the key presence-vs-value collapse and Merlini validated it and split it into three distinct actionable items, bringing the grading fix within reach of closure. [tg:tawg:5061]

> **PR #1932 revocation state converged** — Pavlo and Baby Blue Viper each independently checked the same commit head and confirmed the normative post-revocation label, turning an open question into settled ground. [tg:tawg:5063]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### zkIE / cuda-gkr

_The ZK inference direction gained its first concrete experimental run._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Shipped** a GPT-2 run built around the merged layer-granularity GKR design, translating a conceptual thread into runnable CUDA code and giving the group a real baseline to profile and extend. [tg:tawg:5053]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Shared** the cuda-gkr feature branch, making the implementation directly accessible for collaborative review and iteration. [tg:tawg:5054]

### grading-fix

_The grader correctness work reached a precise and actionable state._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Identified** a remaining boundary in the grading fix: `grade()` using `got.get(k)` collapses a missing key and an explicit null into the same result, which matters for declared-field comparisons and blocks a clean closure of the fix. [tg:tawg:5057]
- Merlini (@gobross) **Validated** Pavlo's analysis and organized the issues into three distinct categories, separating what is actionable immediately from what can be deferred, giving the group a clear path to close the fix without scope creep. [tg:tawg:5061]

### ERC-8373 / PR #1932

_Normative state naming for the post-revocation case was cross-verified and settled._

- Baby Blue Viper **Checked** PR #1932 before the discussion and confirmed the spec text already names the post-revocation state, narrowing the open question before others weighed in. [tg:tawg:5062]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Verified** against the current #1932 head (27e79ea) that the ERC prose already names the post-revocation state, clarifying which definition is normative and anchoring the conversation to settled text. [tg:tawg:5063]
- Baby Blue Viper **Confirmed** the same prose finding against the same commit head and extended the check to `admit()` logic, establishing that resolved-empty and unanchored-chain return distinct named states. [tg:tawg:5064]
- Baby Blue Viper **Resolved** a two-part precision question about `admit()` return values, landing on concrete named states the group can use directly in downstream test and review work. [tg:tawg:5068]

### ERC-8183 / external engagement

_An external perspective arrived in the ongoing specification discussion._

- A procurement-side contribution entered the ERC-8183 thread with a question about Exam design, bringing a mechanism-design angle that widens the context the specification needs to address. [ERC-8183 Magicians post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/422)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Profile the cuda-gkr GPT-2 run to understand where layer-granularity GKR gains or loses on real model shapes
- Explore how the presence-vs-value distinction in the grader maps onto broader grading semantics beyond the immediate fix
- Track whether the Magicians procurement-side question surfaces Exam design constraints worth pulling into the spec

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Land the grader presence-vs-value fix now that the three issues are clearly separated
- Document the settled post-revocation and binding-state terminology from #1932 so test cases can follow
- Review the cuda-gkr branch and give feedback on the GPT-2 CUDA baseline

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** Two contributors independently checked the same PR commit head and arrived at the same normative label — the post-revocation state resolved through dual verification rather than debate.
>
> Turns out the spec already wrote the answer; the group just had to read it twice to be sure. 🔍
